title: Python Package Management and pip Fundamentals
learningObjectives: Explain pip, PyPI, distribution names, import names and python -m pip.
Choose the appropriate package or environment workflow for PY20.1.
Interpret package-management and interpreter information correctly.
Identify dependency, isolation and reproducibility risks.
Apply the concepts in a safe Python project workflow.

understand.concept: pip installs Python distribution packages, commonly from PyPI, into the environment selected by the interpreter. Distribution names can differ from import names. Prefer `python -m pip` so the interpreter and pip target are explicit.
understand.whyItMatters: Package installation adds third-party capabilities while making the target environment clear prevents dependency confusion.
understand.analogy: pip is a delivery service placing a library into a chosen Python workspace.
understand.analogyLimit: Installing a package does not prove that it is trustworthy, compatible or imported under the distribution name.
understand.summary: Python Package Management and pip Fundamentals teaches maintainable dependency management and environment setup.

explain.narrative: Use `python -m pip --version` to identify the pip tied to an interpreter. PyPI is the Python Package Index. A distribution is what package tools install; Python code imports modules or packages that the distribution provides. These names are not guaranteed to match. Installing packages can run build/install steps, so prefer trusted sources and isolated environments.
